test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: After passing a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha can return the bill to the Lok Sabha within a maximum of ______ days.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 14**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rajya Sabha can detain the money bill for the maximum period of 14 days only.
 
• A money bill can only be introduced in Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya sabha. It is introduced only by the minister on the recommendation of the President.
 
• It cannot be amended or rejected by Rajya Sabha and Rajya sabha should return the bill with or without recommendation. The recommendation can be accepted or rejected by Lok Sabha.
 
• It is transmitted to Rajya Sabha after the certification of the Speaker and there is no provision of joint sittings in matters of a money bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Bill

 
 
 
Provision

 
 
 

 
 
Ordinary bill

 
 
 
 
• It can be introduced in both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha and by either minister or a private member of parliament.
 
• It can be amended or rejected by Rajya sabha and can be detained for a period of 6 months.
 
• It is the bill concerned about any matter other than financial subjects.
 
• It is having the provision of joint sittings in case of deadlock and can be returned by the President for further consideration.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Money bill (Article 110)

 
 
 
 
• It is concerned with financial matters like taxation, public expenditure, etc.
 
• It can only introduce in Lok Sabha by the minister with the recommendation of the President.
 
• Rajya Sabha can detain the bill for 14 days and should return the bill with or without recommendation. The recommendations are not binding on Lok Sabha.
 
• It is having no provision of joint sitting and the President cannot return the bill.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Financial bill I (Article 117 {1})

 
 
 
 
• Financial bill is those which concerns with fiscal matters like revenue and expenditure.
 
• This contains matters related to Article 110 and other general legislation also.
 
• It can be introduced only in Lok Sabha after the recommendation of the President.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Financial bill II (Article 117 {3})

 
 
 
 
• This bill contains a matter of expenditure from the consolidated fund of India.
 
• It is governed as same as ordinary bills.
 
• It cannot be passed by either house of Parliament unless the President has recommended to that House the consideration of the bill.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Constitutional amendment bill (Article 368)

 
 
 
 
• It only concerned with the amendment of the provisions of the constitution.
 
• It can be introduced in either house of the parliament and does not require the permission of the President.
 
• It must be passed in each house by the special majority and separately.
 
• It is having no provision of joint sitting and the President cannot hold or return the bill.
